territorial_scope.description: Applies to information made available on interactive computer services and covered platforms, as defined in federal law, from enactment; no explicit extraterritorial reach is stated.

evidence.quote: The amendments made by this Act shall apply to information made available on an interactive computer service

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends Section 230 of the Communications Act to condition its liability shield on providers' reasonable process for cyberstalking and intimate privacy violations, requires covered platforms to remove reported violations within 48 hours, and revises criminal prohibitions on sexually explicit digital forgeries. Introduced; not enacted.
summary.long: Amends Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 so that its general liability protection for interactive computer service providers applies only if the provider runs a reasonable process for cyberstalking and intimate privacy violations, including prevention measures, the TAKE IT DOWN Act notice process, minimum data logging and removal of court-determined unlawful content. Adds generative-model use to content creation under Section 230(f)(3). Revises TAKE IT DOWN Act definitions and criminal prohibitions on sexually explicit digital forgeries. Covered public platforms, excluding broadband, email, messaging and data storage services, must provide a notice-and-removal process and remove reported violations within 48 hours of a valid request; good-faith removal carries liability protection. The FTC, consulting the FCC and as appropriate the Attorney General, must issue implementing regulations within 180 days of enactment. The amendments apply to information made available on or after enactment. The bill is introduced and not enacted.

notes: Introduced bill, text as introduced; no later version in the document. Target instruments are not identified by registry ID, so target_instrument_id is empty. The amendments to section 230(c)(1) and the TAKE IT DOWN Act definitions cite each other (new 230(c)(1)(B)(ii) is cross-referenced by TAKE IT DOWN Act section 4(5) and (6)). Terms are used inconsistently: section 3(b)(1)(B)(4) refers to a nonconsensual intimate privacy violation, a phrase not defined in the text. Section 3(b)(1)(B) also cites subsection (b)(2) for the deletion of subparagraph (D), which is the only exception it removes. Amendments apply to information made available on or after enactment (SEC. 4(b)).

thresholds.note: The bill sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. The 48-hour removal period in Sec. 3(b)(1) (new 47 U.S.C. 223a(a)(3)) and the 180-day rulemaking deadline in Sec. 4(a) are procedural time limits, coded as events rather than thresholds. Definitions of covered platform and covered individual contain no numeric size or age criteria.
